correctness.rationale: Congruence transforms B^T diag(p)B>=gamma I to diag(p)>=gamma (BB^T)^-1. Therefore maximize gamma by minimum-trace diagonal PSD majorant of C; its standard elliptope dual has diag X=1. In the weak branch, the proposed slack quadratic form is an explicit sum of nonnegative squares and its all-ones kernel gives a matching rank-one dual. In the strong branch, slack/w=t vv^T+(1+1/t)L_complete, with v=e_1+e_n-t^-1 sum interiors; matching rank-two correlation X=aa^T+(1-r²)ff^T yields equality. Complementary slackness forces each q uniquely even allowing nonsymmetric competitors; rank of factors proves nullity and t=m/2 boundary. An implicit-function argument starting at C=I establishes feasible unit-row systems for sufficiently small w at every t. Independently checked rational PSD/dual/rank certificates in 64 cases; finite coverage does not replace the symbolic factorization.

evidence: Dai et al. give a generic SDP/approximation, not an all-parameter closed optimizer; Wang et al. use a lifted exact-MSE recursion; inverse-positive SPD quadratic result requires entrywise nonnegative inverse.

originality.rationale: Dai–Soltanalian–Pelckmans establish the general diagonal-majorant SDP, which is prior. The claim evaluates it explicitly for a dense signed complete graph with exactly one negative edge, including unique optimizer, rational strong branch and sharp nullity transition, which were not found in inspected relevant sources. The published inverse-positive-coordinate model assumes nonnegative inverse and is not applicable to negative signed triangles. O=PASS qualified by partially inaccessible 2014 exact-MSE article and possible spin/elliptope literature.

value.rationale: A dense interaction network with one antagonistic coupling is a natural robustness model. The optimizer undergoes a genuine sign-induced structural transition and has explicit probabilities and spectral rate throughout an infinite dimension family, removing a generic semidefinite optimization for this class. The one-step objective is explicitly bounded and avoids unsupported multistep claims.

final_claim: For every unit-row real invertible n-by-n system (n>=5) with inverse row-Gram off-diagonals all +w except one edge -tw, fixed-iid one-step worst-direction expected squared-error contraction has a unique exact probability vector from two explicit diagonal-majorant formulas. Its breakpoint is t=(n-2)/2, with optimal slack nullity changing from one to two.
limitations: Fixed iid sampling and sharp one-step worst-direction conditional expectation only; not exact long-horizon MSE or adaptive methods.
Prescribed C must be compatible with positive-definite unit-row inverse Gram; small w existence is established but arbitrary w existence is not.
